summary:
TerraLens: Local Climate Intelligence for Smarter Agriculture*

TerraLens is a web-based climate intelligence platform that transforms NASA Earth science data into understandable, locally relevant insights to support agricultural planning in Kadingilan, Bukidnon. Using historical climate data from NASA POWER, the platform presents variables such as precipitation, temperature, and relative humidity through interactive dashboards, historical comparisons, and trend analysis.

TerraLens addresses the challenge of understanding how environmental variables change over time and how these trends may differ across locations. By making climate patterns easier to explore and interpret, it helps the Municipal Agriculture Office, farmers, and other local stakeholders gain a clearer understanding of historical environmental conditions that may affect agricultural activities.

This project is important because access to understandable climate information can support more informed agricultural planning, strengthen local awareness of environmental changes, and encourage data-informed decision-making. TerraLens connects global Earth science data with local agricultural needs, turning complex environmental information into practical insights.
details:
Q1. What does it do or how does it work? What benefits does it have?

TerraLens is a web-based local climate intelligence platform designed to help the Municipality of Kadingilan, Bukidnon, particularly its Municipal Agriculture Office, understand historical environmental changes and use this information to support agricultural planning.

The platform uses NASA's Prediction of Worldwide Energy Resources (POWER) API to access historical meteorological data, focusing on precipitation, temperature, and relative humidity. It processes and visualizes these datasets through interactive dashboards, allowing users to explore environmental conditions, compare different years and seasons, and identify long-term trends.

TerraLens also aims to connect climate information with verified local agricultural resources, such as crop calendars, planting schedules, and agricultural records. Through its AI-assisted research interface, users can ask questions about the available environmental data and receive understandable explanations based on actual analysis and reliable references.

Its main benefits include making complex Earth science data easier to access and understand, helping local government personnel examine historical climate patterns, and providing farmers and agricultural stakeholders with additional information for agricultural planning and research.

Q2. What is the intended impact of the project?

TerraLens aims to bridge the gap between global Earth science data and the information needs of local agricultural communities.

Our initial focus is Kadingilan, Bukidnon, where the platform is intended to support the Municipal Agriculture Office in understanding historical climate patterns and making environmental information more accessible to local farmers.

The project seeks to contribute to:

  • Better-informed agricultural planning: Provide historical climate information that can be considered alongside crop calendars and local agricultural knowledge.
  • Improved access to environmental information: Make NASA-derived datasets easier for local government personnel and agricultural stakeholders to explore.
  • Stronger local research capabilities: Help the LGU examine long-term environmental trends and investigate their possible relationships with agricultural conditions.
  • Farmer awareness and information access: Make understandable climate summaries and relevant agricultural information more accessible to farming communities.
  • Scalable local impact: Establish a platform that could eventually be adapted for other municipalities in Bukidnon and other agricultural communities.

Ultimately, TerraLens aims to help local communities make more informed decisions by transforming environmental data into meaningful and accessible insights.

Q3. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

TerraLens is being developed as a web-based software platform that integrates NASA Earth science data with data processing, statistical analysis, interactive visualization, and AI-assisted explanations.

Our primary external data source is the NASA POWER API, which provides historical meteorological information used in the platform.

The development technologies include:

NASA POWER API: Source of historical precipitation, temperature, and relative humidity data.

  • Frontend: React and Vite
  • Programming languages: JSON, HTML, and CSS.
  • Backend and data processing: Node.js, using JavaScript ES modules and a built-in HTTP server. It retrieves NASA POWER data and calculates climate statistics.
  • Data visualization: Apache ECharts for charts, Leaflet for interactive maps, and Three.js for the 3D Earth globe.
  • Artificial intelligence: Google Gemini API, using the gemini-3.1-flash-lite model by default. The model can be configured through GEMINI_MODEL.
  • Development tools: Visual Studio Code, Git, GitHub, and Vite for local development and frontend builds.
  • Deployment: Vercel

The platform primarily relies on software and publicly accessible environmental datasets, so no specialized physical hardware is required for its core functionality.

Q4. How is your project creative? What factors did your team consider?

What makes TerraLens creative is its approach of transforming global environmental datasets into locally relevant information for a specific community.

NASA produces valuable Earth science data, but these datasets can be difficult for non-specialists to interpret and apply. Instead of simply displaying raw environmental measurements, TerraLens combines interactive geographic visualization, historical trend analysis, statistical methods, and AI-assisted explanations to make the information more understandable and useful.

Our team considered several important factors when developing the concept:

  • Local relevance: We selected Kadingilan, Bukidnon, as our initial focus to address the information needs of a real agricultural community.
  • Accessibility: We wanted to make complex environmental datasets understandable to local government personnel and agricultural stakeholders, including users without specialized data science backgrounds.
  • Scientific reliability: We considered the importance of using credible NASA data sources, validating datasets, applying appropriate statistical methods, and avoiding unsupported conclusions.
  • Practical application: We designed the concept around agricultural planning and local research rather than limiting it to environmental data visualization.
  • Scalability: We considered how the platform could eventually incorporate local agricultural records, farmer observations, and additional environmental datasets, and expand to other municipalities.
  • Responsible use of AI: We intend for AI to explain and contextualize actual data and verified references, rather than generate unsupported agricultural recommendations or predictions.

TerraLens demonstrates how Earth science data, technology, and local knowledge can work together to address community-level challenges.

Our vision is simple - "See the Earth. Understand the Change. Empower the Future".
